newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wheat pool unchanged at A$185/t. [CORRECTED 7:56 GMT]
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wheat pool unchanged at A$185/t. [CORRECTED 7:56 GMT]

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Monday it will leave unchanged at A$185 a tonne, fob, its estimated pool returns for Australian Standard White (ASW) wheat.
(Wheat Board corrects price in headline and first paragraph from A$180/t)
For durum wheat, the estimated return for all grades rose by A$5 a tonne, with the durum number one pool now expected to return A$260 a tonne, fob, the AWB said.
The estimates are for the current 1996/97 harvest.
The AWB said earlier on Monday that 18.5 million tonnes of the estimated 21.5 million tonnes of production in the 1996/97 harvest had been delivered to the AWB pools.
"In a harvest as large as as this, the influence of the pool on the domestic market is even more pronounced," AWB merchandiing manager Philip Pyle said in a statement.

"The pool is at least 20 percent bigger than any we've handled since deregulation, but we've made great strides in marketing what may yet prove to be our largest wheat crop," he said. The AWB controls Australia's export sales of wheat.
Pyle said that because the United States was not offering export subsidies for wheat it was benefiting Australian farmers.
Moreover, grains buyers worldwide were changing their buying patterns, and looking to make fewer forward purchases.
"It's rare now to see a customer want to price grain more than two months forward and even the large scale customers are pricing smaller quantities of wheat than usual," Pyle said.
The next revision date for pool returns is scheduled for January 20, the AWB said.
